Terrain editing: Phase 0 report

Done Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-23 Source: terrain-editing-phase-0.md

What the foundation of the terrain editor is, as built: the tile model, the stroke engine, the native .terrain container, regional GI and the brush cursor, with the C ABI that carries them, how each piece is verified, the decisions behind it and what is left. The plan itself is in terrain-editing-roadmap.md.

1. What Phase 0 delivered#

PieceWhereWhat it does
Tile modelsrc/caffeine/terrain/edit/TerrainTiles.*Tiles of 64 cells that own disjoint vertices; dirty tiles and the changed region; integer-centimetre coordinates; 16-bit centimetre height tiles with an exact float fallback
Stroke engineterrain/edit/TerrainStroke.*Stamps spaced in metres along a path; five modes; stamp images, falloff curves, rotation, a pressure hook; tile-by-tile undo records
Native containerterrain/TerrainContainer.*A caf asset of type Terrain: a tile directory and one CRC-checked record per tile; partial loading; lossless conversion of a legacy .cterrain
Convertercaf-pack --convert-terrain, convertLegacyTerrainReads a .cterrain, writes the .terrain, reads it back and compares bit for bit before it reports success
Cacheterrain/TerrainCache.*commitHeightEdit (local mesh rebuild), per-tile revisions, giTilesFor, dataFileIsLegacy, convertToNative, saveNativeTerrainFile
Regional GIrender/GpuSceneRenderer.cppA terrain is one Photon object per tile with its own revision, so a stroke revoxelises only the tiles it touched
C ABIcapi/EngineAPI.*Versions 25 (strokes), 26 (data format, conversion) and 27 (terrain raycast, brush outline)
Editordoppio/crates/ui, doppio/crates/engineRust wrappers; the brush cursor overlay; Scene > Convert terrains to .terrain; the convert_terrains and terrain_brush_cursor agent actions

2. The tile model#

  • A terrain of N vertices has ceil((N-1)/64) tiles a side (257 is 4, 4097 is 64). A tile owns its vertices (the last tile of a row also owns the final one), so tiles never overlap; its mesh region is the owned vertices plus one on every side.
  • A point is also named in integer centimetres from the corner (vertexXCm), the form a stable id is hashed from: resampling the heightmap does not change it, and a kilometre-wide terrain is addressed by tile first and a small offset after.
  • DirtyTiles keeps the tiles an edit touched and the tight rectangle of vertices that really changed; the mesh and the GI grow that rectangle by one vertex themselves.
  • quantizeHeights stores a tile as 16-bit offsets of 1 cm from a base (655 m of range); a tile that does not fit keeps its floats.

3. The stroke engine#

  • A stroke is a path of points. The brush is laid on it as stamps spaced a fixed number of metres apart, never one per frame: the same path gives the same terrain at 2 or 240 samples. Radius, spacing and heights are metres; positions are metres from the terrain's centre.
  • Raise, lower and noise change the height by metres per stamp; smooth and flatten move a 0 to 1 share toward the average or the target. Smoothing reads a copy of the region, so the result does not depend on the order of vertices. Noise is deterministic for a seed.
  • The first touch of a tile copies its heights; finish returns a StrokeRecord with before and after for the tiles that really changed. Undo and redo are bit-exact, and the record is a few tiles even on an 8 km terrain.

4. The native .terrain container#

PartContent
Header (32 B)caf magic 0xCAFECAFE, type Terrain, CRC32 of the payload
MetadataTerrainFileMeta (format version 1, resolution, extent in metres, maximum height), the mask directory, and the tile directory (offset, size and CRC32 of every tile)
PayloadOne record per tile, rows then columns, each 16-byte aligned: the heights, the splat weights of the splat texels the tile owns, and the same sub-rectangle of every stored mask
FooterCRC32 of the whole file
Lossless ruleA height tile is 16-bit only when decoding returns every float bit for bit (so NaN, infinities, -0 and relief above 655 m stay as floats); splat weights are bytes only when every weight is exactly byte/255, otherwise four floats; masks are 8 bits already
Readeropen reads the header and directories; loadTile, loadTilesInto read only the tiles asked for and check each CRC; verifyWholeFile checks the footer; a failed load leaves the caller's maps untouched
Opening old projectsloadTerrainAny detects the format by signature (CTRN is legacy); a legacy terrain opens as it is and is flagged, and nativeTerrainPath gives the .terrain path to offer

5. C ABI#

VersionFunctionsPurpose
25caffeine_session_terrain_stroke_begin / _point / _end / _revert / _reapplyA stroke on a terrain entity: points in world space, a local mesh rebuild per point, one collision-mesh refresh per stroke, undo records within a 512 MB budget
26caffeine_session_terrain_data_legacy, caffeine_session_terrain_convert_nativeWhether a terrain is still in the old format; save it as .terrain, checked bit for bit, and point the scene at it (the old file stays)
27caffeine_session_terrain_raycast, caffeine_session_terrain_brush_outlineWhere a ray meets a terrain, and the ring a brush makes on the relief

6. Regional GI#

  • Photon built one object for a terrain, so any edit revoxelised all of it, and a terrain made of chunks (the default) was not voxelised at all because it has no single mesh. A terrain is now cut into tiles; each tile has a coarse mesh and a revision that moves only when an edit touched it.
  • The mesh step keeps the whole terrain within 400 000 triangles and cells of at least about a metre (the voxel volume resolves no more). The boxes of neighbouring terrain tiles are merged, because the voxeliser rebuilds a level whole when it gets more than eight boxes; boxes of ordinary objects are not merged, so a scene that changed wholesale still rebuilds whole and the light settles again.
  • Not done yet: precompiled GI per region stored in the container. Phase 5.

7. Verification#

  • C++: tests/test_terrain_edit.cpp (tiles, strokes, golden fingerprints for the five modes, a per-stamp budget of about 0.03 to 0.05 ms that does not grow with the terrain, GI tiles, opening and converting a legacy terrain), tests/test_terrain_container.cpp (10 cases) and the C ABI cases in tests/test_capi.cpp. The whole suite: 1099 cases.
  • Rust: the engine-crate test of a stroke and its undo; photon_gi::a_terrain_stroke_revoxelises_only_the_tiles_it_touched (16 objects, no whole rebuild, at most 8 boxes); terrain_format (an old project is reported, converted and reopened bit for bit); terrain_cursor (the ring follows the mouse and hugs the relief). The whole suite: 590 tests, clippy with and without the agent feature, ./scripts/check-rust-ui.sh.

8. Decisions recorded#

  • Material layers: up to 64 per palette, 4 blended per texel, resolution per layer, a layered or a simple mode per terrain; only what a camera can see stays loaded.
  • Vegetation: procedural and manual are both placement sources, switchable without losing data; the target is 1M instances in real units (per hectare), so GPU culling, LOD and impostors are in Phase 3.
  • Real metric units everywhere (cm, m, km); stable ids come from integer-centimetre world coordinates; a legacy terrain converts without losing a bit; the partial update of the physics collider is out of scope; tablet pressure is Phase 5 (the stroke already carries a pressure and the brush a hook).

9. Known limits and what is next#

  • A conversion is a file-format migration, not an undoable edit; the engine marks the scene changed so that saving keeps it. saveTerrainFile with a .terrain path returns false on purpose (it lacks the extent and height scale); scenes use saveNativeTerrainFile.
  • The brush cursor has no button yet: the agent action and the tests turn it on, and the Terrain Editor of Phase 1 will. A stroke point reaches the engine in world space through a float matrix, which will be revisited with camera-relative rendering for terrains far from the origin.
  • Vegetation tiles and precompiled GI in the container belong to Phases 3 and 5. Next: Phase 1, the brush library (.brush, about 40 procedural brushes, every mode, protection mask, symmetry) and the Terrain Editor UI.

10. Work log#

  • 2026-11-22: the plan and its decisions were written (terrain-editing-roadmap.md); the tile model, the stroke engine, C ABI 25 and the Rust wrapper were built. The session Container .terrain and converter built the container and the caf-pack converter in parallel, in files this session did not touch.
  • 2026-11-23: the golden and budget tests, regional GI, the legacy-terrain prompt and conversion (C ABI 26) and the brush cursor (C ABI 27) closed the phase. Incidents: a git stash in the website submodule was undone at once without conflicts; /tmp filled up twice and only old test artifacts were removed; merging every dirty Photon box broke the thin-wall GI test, which is why only terrain tiles are merged.
